match.reason: No point in the bank teaches market research; the closest, customers, suppliers and competitors, explains how those groups influence a business rather than how to research them before spending money.

draft.title: Market research for a new business
card: Market research is collecting and studying information about a market before a business is started. It is done before money is spent, so mistakes cost less.
It asks four things: who the customers are, what they want, what competitors already offer, and whether enough people will buy.
new information the owner collects first-hand, such as a survey, an interview or a trial sample.
information that already exists, such as government population data, industry reports or competitor websites.
draft.remember: Research first to learn who will buy, what they want and who else sells to them.

a.q: Why should an owner do market research before spending money on a new business?
opts: To learn whether enough customers are likely to buy
To make sure the business will never face competitors
To avoid the need for a plan for finance and staff
To guarantee that the business makes a profit
a.why: Research gives evidence about customers, their wants and competitors, so the owner can judge demand before risking money. It cannot guarantee profit, because results can still turn out differently from what research suggests.
a.clue: Think about what the owner wants to know before risking money.

b.q: Priya plans a juice bar in Orange. She reads council data on how many people work nearby, then asks 50 passers-by what drinks they would buy. Which describes her research?
opts: Secondary research from the data, primary from the questions
Primary research from the data, secondary from the questions
Both parts are secondary research, as others will buy
Both parts are primary research, as they relate to her bar
b.why: The council data already existed, so it is secondary research. Asking passers-by collects new information first-hand, so it is primary. Relating to her own bar does not make existing data primary.
b.clue: Ask who collected each piece of information, and when.

a.best: To learn whether enough customers are likely to buy

b.best: Secondary research from the data, primary from the questions

problems.detail: The card defines market research as collecting information 'before a business is started'. Established businesses also do market research all the time, so as a general definition this is too narrow. Wording such as 'For a new business, market research is done before it starts' would fix it.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is that the card's definition suggests market research happens only before a business starts, which is too narrow.
